ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md` again, as the skill requires before every fix round, to confirm who fixes round 5, how the scoped re-review runs, and the adjudication rule after the fifth attempt.

ACTION: Dispatch the round 5 fix subagent with model `fable`. The implementer is already at capable (opus), and round 4 was a thorough attempt that still failed, so `fable` is the next rung and the Agent tool lists it. The prompt is built per fix-loop.md: the Task 6 brief file from `scripts/task-brief`, the global constraints copied verbatim from the plan, and finding F1 verbatim (the invalidation races with the background refresh at `cache/refresh.py:88`, and the new test passes only because it never starts the refresh thread). It also names the round 4 report file so the subagent can see what was already tried. It asks for a fix that holds when the refresh thread actually runs, plus a test that starts the refresh thread and fails without the fix. It does not pre-rate severity or tell the subagent what not to touch.

ACTION: After the fix lands, write the review package for the new commits and dispatch the scoped re-review (`re-review-prompt.md`) with the diff file path. If F1 is still open after this fifth attempt, I adjudicate per fix-loop.md. Otherwise I append the Task 6 line to the ledger.

Message to partner:

Task 6's re-review still reports Important finding F1: the invalidation races with the background refresh at `cache/refresh.py:88`, and the new test passes only because it never starts the refresh thread. Four fix attempts have not closed it, so I'm dispatching round 5, the last allowed, at `fable` with the finding and the earlier attempt's report. A scoped re-review follows.
